page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v6 is an x86_64 server instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory configuration is 64.0 GB, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance includes a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD and is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32alds_v6 demonstrates strong single-core and multi-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for Geekbench single-core, multi-core, and stress-ng single-core tests. Its cryptographic capabilities are also strong, reflected in the top 25% PassMark CPU encryption score, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions. Memory performance is robust, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25%, though large-block memory bandwidth reads and writes fall into the middle 50% average. For specialized workloads, it achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small LLM models, while medium and large model inference speeds remain average.

The server's hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff: it offers high compute density and substantial local NVMe storage, but is constrained by a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2. This makes it a cost-efficient option for compute-heavy tasks that require fast local scratch space but do not demand massive memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include text and image processing, software compilation, web serving, and database operations that fit within the 64.0 GB memory limit.
